note: Skeptic Shark, operator angle. Judged only against the locked surfaces — open the step and click, always a register link, Run stages a command in an Anchor window — not against the codebase.

findings.criterion: 4 — a Run link opens a cockpit terminal … an Anchor window, token-gated; 5 — a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: Wave 2's Open link appends the page token the way the file link already does. Wave 6 then window.opens `/terminal?session=<sid>` and never mentions `token`. The W6.2 HOLD even asks whether the existing standalone page is reachable "with session+token as-is" — then the near-term URL drops the token. GET terminal transports are already 401-before-substance. He clicks Run ▶, a window opens, and it is blank. Criterion 4's Anchor window never appears; criterion 5's screenshot is an empty page. Carry the token the same way Open does. The alias is not the fix.

findings.criterion: 5 — Nothing regresses, and it is seen — steward/cockpit nets stay green; a Gandalf run is opened from the plan outline AND the deliverables tile; a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: The only machine-countable ship gate names `tests/test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`, a file no wave creates. It omits every new file the waves actually ship: the W1 containment stub gate, the W3 registrar/concurrency/round-trip tests, the W5/W6 Run-terminal tests, and the W7 Playwright file (`importorskip('playwright')` even if someone adds it). Foreman can go green on three old nets plus a missing path while the outline click-through, the Run window, and the hostile-Where fixtures never run. Criterion 5 is a claim about John's page. A gate that cannot see that page is how a green branch ships a dead click.

findings.criterion: 1 — When a Gandalf run finalizes, a researchPrime / lane job finishes, or a Foreman wave GOes, one row is appended; Statement — a Foreman execution log appears as a clickable link
findings.message: Criterion 1 names three finish events. The plan then (a) filters Hook B to `lane in ('research','plan')` so a classic build job writes nothing, (b) registers the execution log only on commissioned `finish_run` (Hook C), and (c) parks the only wave-GO writer (P2.8) behind a Stage-2 question. A Foreman run from the project window — the path the risk table itself keeps in scope — still leaves the outline and the tile empty. Per-wave GO never mints a row. Asking John to re-decide a locked criterion is not a HOLD of extra machinery; the third named finish event is still fiction. Commit a Foreman writer on the paths criterion 1 named, or amend the North Star.

findings.criterion: 1 — the row carries the roadmap step it belongs to (the active step at the time); 3 — the plan outline's step expansion lists the step's register rows
findings.message: The surface he locked is: open the roadmap step, click the report. Wave 3 will fill Step from `active_step` when the hint is omitted — at register time, after finalize. Hook C stamps the commission's step at launch. Hook A (Gandalf, the leading example) and Hook B pass no hint. If the step is no longer `active` when the hook fires — already done, or the next step now active — the row lands under the wrong step or under none. Wave 4's Gandalf Given/When/Then never asserts the Step cell at all, so Foreman can ship the named path with an outline join that the tile hides. Stamp the step at launch (Hook C already does), and assert it on the Gandalf fixture.

findings.topic: shell pending-paste flushes on first bytes
findings.criterion: 4 — the command staged as a pending paste, Enter runs it; 5 — Playwright shows the command sitting unsent on the prompt
findings.message: Criterion 4/5 require a clean command on the prompt so Enter runs it. For `backend=='shell'` the flush is "the PTY produced its first output bytes." A Windows PowerShell/`COMSPEC` banner is output that is not a prompt. Flushing raw command bytes into the banner means he does not see a staged line — and may not have a runnable command on the prompt at all. The existing greet-gated flush exists because "any output" is the wrong gate. Wave 5's stub PTY has no banner; Wave 7's live screenshot will either fail honestly or be skipped (Finding 2). Name an idle-prompt detector before claiming Enter-to-run.

findings.topic: Run cwd is effort dir not project tree
findings.criterion: 4 — a cockpit terminal in the project's tree with the command staged, Enter to run
findings.message: The locked Run behavior is a terminal in the project's tree. Wave 5 hedges "project tree or a caller-supplied effort dir"; Wave 6 then sets cwd to "that row's effort dir when the row is effort-level." A `run: python tools/foo.py` written against the project root fails on Enter when cwd is `planning/…/effort`. He pressed Enter; it did not run. That is the operator failure criterion 4 exists to prevent. Allowlist the command; cwd is the project folder the North Star named, unless the row itself declares otherwise.

findings.criterion: 3 — a report registered with a step shows in the plan outline; the deliverables tile always shows it
findings.message: The risk table sends a run with no effort to the project root. Hook B does not call `effort_dir_for`. It uses `rec.get('effort_dir') or project root`, and the `effort_dir` passthrough is optional with "no behavior change when absent" and no caller named. The plan outline reads the effort's `DELIVERABLES.md`. A project that has an effort — the case he works in — then shows the classic-window report in the project-root list, not under the step he opens. Criterion 3 is both places, not "whichever file the project-wide pane happens to read." Wire the passthrough on the launch paths that have an effort, or those reports stay missing from the outline.

findings.topic: registrar miss is silent on the page
findings.criterion: 1 — a finished run registers itself (one row is appended); 5 — it is seen
findings.message: Criterion 1 is a row appearing; criterion 5 is that he can click it. `register()` never raises; the only observer of `written:false` is a journal field `{register: written|dup|reason}` he does not read. A finish that no-ops leaves the outline and the tile exactly as they are today — no link — with no cockpit signal. Best-effort is right (a registrar exception must not fail the job). Operator-visible success cannot be only a journal field. Surface the miss on the effort, or fail the Wave 7 dogfood when the row is absent; otherwise "it is seen" is unenforceable the first time a hook no-ops in production.

findings.topic: Hook B and Hook C double-register
findings.criterion: 1 — when a researchPrime / lane job finishes, one row is appended
findings.message: Idempotency is on exact `(what, where)`. Hook B writes `'<researchPrime|Crucible> <lane> report — <label>'` at `/report/<pid>/<lane>/<job_id>`. Hook C writes `'<skill> — <role>: <filename>'` at the session-doc path. A commissioned researchPrime that also `_finalize`s a lane job is one run minting two rows with two labels and two Wheres. He opens the step and sees the same report twice. The plan never says Hook B skips commissioned jobs. One finish event, one row — pick a writer per path, or the register stops being a click target.

findings.criterion: 3 — Both places, one source — the pane and the plan outline render the same register rows as links
findings.message: The register is one source; the paint is still two. `delivRow` emits the tokenized `<a target=_blank>`. `loadDeliv` gets a separate `window.open(route + token)` branch. The plan already admits that leaving `loadDeliv` unpatched makes the same row a link in the tile and dead text in the other list. That failure returns the day the copies diverge. Make `loadDeliv` call `delivRow` (or one helper). Two hand-kept route branches are how one of the two places goes dark.

findings.topic: Run window is Zombie Hunter page
findings.criterion: 4 — a Run link opens … an Anchor window (a cockpit terminal in the project's tree)
findings.message: He clicks Run ▶ and, if the alias is cut, lands on the existing standalone page behind `/zombie_terminal` — a window whose object is Zombie Hunter, not the command he just staged. The HOLD's question is already answered by that page taking `session`+`token`. A second route to the same page retires nothing. If the existing URL is used, retitle by session kind; do not ship a Run control that opens the hunter.
